aliases: faa recreational pilot knowledge test rpt

domains.name: Applicable Federal Aviation Regulations of this chapter that relate to recreational pilot privileges, limitations, and flight operations
Accident reporting requirements of the National Transportation Safety Board
Use of the applicable portions of the Aeronautical Information Manual and FAA advisory circulars
Use of aeronautical charts for VFR navigation using pilotage with the aid of a magnetic compass
Recognition of critical weather situations from the ground and in flight, windshear avoidance, and the procurement and use of aeronautical weather reports and forecasts
Safe and efficient operation of aircraft, including collision avoidance, and recognition and avoidance of wake turbulence
Effects of density altitude on takeoff and climb performance
Principles of aerodynamics, powerplants, and aircraft systems
Stall awareness, spin entry, spins, and spin recovery techniques, if applying for an airplane single-engine rating

exam_rules: FAA-approved test supplements provided at testing center. Approved calculators and flight computers permitted. E6B flight computer (mechanical or electronic) allowed. No personal electronic devices. No personal notes or reference materials.
id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required. Student pilot certificate or instructor endorsement required for some tests. Name on ID must match registration exactly.

lifecycle.summary: Confirmed current on the issuer host on 2026-09-20: "This subpart prescribes the requirement for the issuance of recreational pilot certificates and ratings, the conditions under which those certificates and ratings are necessary, and the general operating rules for persons who hold those certificates and ratings."

passing_score_scale: Percentage (70% passing for all knowledge tests)
renewal_options: FAA Airman certificates do not expire, but proficiency requirements apply. Airman Knowledge Test result valid for 24 months for scheduling the practical test (checkride). Pilots must complete a Biennial Flight Review (BFR) every 24 months to act as PIC. Currency requirements (landings, instrument approaches) are separate from certificate renewal.

retake_policy.notes: 14-day waiting period required after a failed attempt. No limit on total number of attempts. Instructor endorsement or authorized sign-off required before retaking.

testing_centers.notes: All FAA Airman Knowledge Tests administered at PSI/CATS authorized testing centers. No online proctoring available. Schedule at faa.psiexams.com or call PSI at 1-800-211-2753.
testing_centers.provider: PSI Exams (CATS — Computer Assisted Testing Service)
